name: Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple, Melukote
deity: Vishnu as Cheluvanarayana (Thirunarayana), with the hilltop shrine of Yoga Narasimha
period: The sacred hill of Yadugiri, seat of Ramanuja's Sri Vaishnava revival, famed for the Vairamudi crown
summary: On the hill of Yadugiri, Vishnu is worshipped as Cheluvanarayana at a temple made great by Ramanuja, who lived here years; once a year the god wears the diamond Vairamudi, the crown no eye may see put on.

sections.history: Melukote crowns the rocky hill of Yadugiri in the Mandya country of Karnataka. The temple of Cheluvanarayana rose to fame through Ramanuja, the great Sri Vaishnava teacher, who lived here for some years and organised its worship; on the hilltop above stands the older shrine of Yoga Narasimha.
sections.architecture: The town is built up the terraced hill in the Dravidian manner, its temple tanks and stepped ponds famous, the Cheluvanarayana shrine below and the Narasimha temple crowning the summit. The setting of rock, water, and sky is inseparable from the pilgrimage.
sections.legends: The image of Cheluvanarayana, called Ramapriya, is said to have been worshipped by Rama and then by Krishna, lost, and recovered by Ramanuja through a vision. The Vairamudi, a crown of diamonds held to be of divine origin, is placed on the god only in darkness, unseen — its keeping the temple's deepest secret.
sections.festivals: The Vairamudi festival is the great occasion, when the diamond crown is brought under guard and set on the god, drawing vast crowds up the hill. Through the year Melukote keeps the Sri Vaishnava calendar in the tradition Ramanuja shaped.
sections.experience: Melukote is a place of steep steps, temple ponds, and long views over the plain — a pilgrimage bound to the memory of Ramanuja, most intense on the night the unseen diamond crown is worn.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening worship and a midday break; the Vairamudi festival is by far the busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Melukote lies in Mandya district of Karnataka, reached by road from Mysuru and Bengaluru, the nearest railhead being Mandya.
